12. Plaint has not been incorporated in the paper book, but from the judgment of the trial Court it appears that the suit was filed for declaration that the initiation of vested property Case No. 9 of 1984 (KDA) and the notice issued in the said case on 27.09.1984 asking the plaintiffs to hand over possession of the suit property was illegal, without jurisdiction and also for a mandatory injunction to restore back possession of the suit property to the plaintiffs. From the findings of the trial Court it further appears that plaintiff No.  1 as P.W.1 admitted in his cross-examination that the Government took over possession of the suit property from them by force in 1984. The trial Court further found that after taking possession of the suit property the Government leased out the same to defendant No. 3 on 29.10.1984, whereas the suit was filed on 03.11.1984, so the plaintiffs having been dispossessed from the suit property before filing of the suit they were required to pray for recovery of khas possession as per the provisions of section 42 of the Act. In coming to the above findings, the trial Court also noticed that the plaintiffs filed an application for amendment of the plaint on 28.10.1999 adding the prayer for restoration of possession of the suit property by mandatory injunction which was allowed by the Court on 25.11.1999 on averments to the effect 

 13. The trial Court further found that the general power of attorney given by Dilip Kumar Roy; a lessee in favour of Kawsar Uddin on 27.07.1956 who transferred the suit property to Mahmuda Begum, vendor of the plaintiffs was not legal and by virtue of such transfer Mahmuda Begum did not acquire any title to the suit property, so also the plaintiffs by their purchase from Mahmuda Begum by the 3(three) kabalas dated 09.06.1969. Moreover, the said kabalas were not proved as per the rules of evidence. With the above findings the trial Court came to the conclusion that the plaintiffs having been dispossessed prior to the filing of the suit their suit without the prayer for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession was not maintainable in law, in view of the provision of section 42 of the Act. From the judgment of the appellate Court it appears that it did not reverse the findings of the trial Court as to the maintainability of the suit and in fact, it decreed the suit mainly on the view that after the repeal of Ordinance No. 1 of 1969 on 23.03.1974 no property could be treated as vested and non-resident properly. It further appears that the appellate Court also found title of the plaintiffs in the suit property on the basis of adverse possession although admittedly from 09.06.1969 till the filing of the suit on 03.11.1984 only 14 years elapsed and title by adverse possession against the Government cannot accrue before expiry of 60 years. From the judgment of the High Court Division it appears that the learned Judge did not at all consider the findings given by the trial Court particularly as to the maintainability of the suit in the light of the provision of section 42 of the Act and in a very casual manner after quoting the findings of the two Courts below affirmed those of the appellate Court. 

 II. Whether the learned Judge of the High Court Division was justified in making the Rule absolute affirming the judgment and decree passed by the appellate Court inasmuch as the plaintiffs suit without prayer for recovery of khas possession was not maintainable in law in view of the finding of the trial Court that they were dispossessed from the suit property before filing of the suit.
